clue.text: Period History reached in 1066 and All That

definitions.meaning: the punctuation mark that closes a sentence

definitions.text: History reached in 1066 and All That
definitions.meaning: the comic British history book 1066 and All That ends with the line 'History came to a .', the dot standing for the stop

explanation.walkthrough: 1066 and All That (1930) is a famous British spoof of school history; its last line has history coming to a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a period is the dot ending a sentence, the same mark British writers call by this name.

clue.text: Very many meet up north for a change

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Lots of people gather in the north for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges MEET, UP and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for an unspecified large number.

clue.text: One quid, what it's given for — cereal or sweet?

parts.note: a quid is a pound, abbreviated L from the Latin libra
I is the Roman numeral one
in 'quid pro quo' a quid is given for a quo
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A pound coin buys a choice between breakfast cereal and confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One quid' gives I and L; the Latin phrase quid pro quo supplies QUO. Liquorice is a black chewy sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquorice is a chewy black confection flavoured with the root of the same name.

clue.text: Boring thing, a snare

definitions.meaning: a surgeon's tool that bores holes in the skull
an old word for a trap or to entrap someone

explanation.definitionFit: A trepan is a cylindrical saw for drilling the skull, and archaically a trick or trap.

clue.text: Go all reactionary when summertime's over

definitions.meaning: to return to old ways and undo progress
what is done to clocks when British Summer Time ends in autumn

explanation.definitionFit: Turning back the hands is a figure for reversing progress, and literally what clocks need each autumn.

clue.text: One that prays for flies?

parts.note: an insect that holds its forelegs as if in prayer, and preys on flies: 'prays' sounds like the hunting word

explanation.walkthrough: The insect is called 'praying' for its folded forelegs; the pun on preying explains the flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying insect folds its front legs as though at worship and hunts small flying insects.

clue.text: Desecrate tomb of old German nobleman

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or deface
a grave is a tomb

explanation.surface: Vandals spoil the burial place of an old German aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A margrave was a hereditary military governor in the Holy Roman Empire, a count of a border province.

clue.text: Motorists so impatient in south-west London?

explanation.definitionFit: Impatient drivers keep sounding their horns, and Tooting is a London district in the borough of Wandsworth.

clue.text: Learned to describe Arnold's wandering youth

definitions.meaning: Matthew Arnold's poem The Scholar-Gipsy tells of an Oxford student who wandered off with gypsies

explanation.walkthrough: Arnold is the Victorian poet Matthew Arnold; his wandering young man is the Scholar-Gipsy, so the adjective fits him.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarly means academic and erudite, the quality of a student.

clue.text: Pop a question if part is not clear

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the letters lie inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A suitor is unsure whether to propose if things are murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' signals that the letters run inside 'Pop a question'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opaque lets no light through, so it is murky or hard to understand.

clue.text: Terrible trash — show disapproval in this Egyptian style

indicators.note: the jeer is placed inside the rearranged letters
something terrible is mangled, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: to show disapproval is to boo

explanation.surface: A critic jeers at shoddy Egyptian fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' looks like a verdict on the hat; it is the anagram signal, and 'in' is the container. A tarboosh is the Egyptian name for a fez.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarboosh is a brimless red cap like a fez, worn in Egypt and the Middle East.

clue.text: Irishman one put back in church's empty' tomb

indicators.note: the reversed pieces are placed inside the letters for church

parts.note: CH is a standard abbreviation for church

indicators.note: put back means the words are written in reverse order of letters

parts.note: Pat (Patrick) is the stock Irishman's name in crosswords
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Irishman is laid back in a church's vacant grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns PATONE into ENOTAP, which goes inside CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a monument to people buried elsewhere, so it holds no body.

clue.text: Ordered for second round by boxing official, wrongly

parts.note: a referee, or ref, officiates a boxing match
ill can mean badly or wrongly, as in ill-judged

explanation.surface: A rematch is ordered after a boxing referee gets it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second round' suggests boxing, but here it is a second round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A refill is a further glassful, the drink you order when another round is called.

clue.text: Slow mover would not join the dance

definitions.meaning: a creature famous for crawling slowly
in Lewis Carroll's Lobster Quadrille the creature 'would not, could not join the dance'

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition quotes the Lobster Quadrille in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is the proverbial slowcoach, and Carroll's Mock Turtle sings of one refusing the dance.

clue.text: Burden the horrid old woman with horse equipment

parts.note: to saddle someone is to burden them
bag is a derogatory word for an unpleasant old woman

explanation.surface: Someone loads an unpleasant old woman with tack for riding.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddlebag is a pouch hung from a horse's saddle, part of riding gear.

clue.text: Street-cleaner, to wit one of the Furies?

parts.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for 'namely' or 'to wit'
the Furies of Greek myth were avenging spirits

explanation.surface: A street-sweeper is likened to an avenging spirit from myth.
explanation.walkthrough: In older English a scavenger was a person employed to clean the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a scavenger was the person paid to clear refuse from the streets.

clue.text: New ale curing such a headache?

indicators.note: making something new here means remaking the letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fresh brew is said to cure a hangover headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges ALE CURING.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is sharp nerve pain, so a nerve-pain headache is so described.

clue.text: Fish for the holy man, soberly clad

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
dressed in gray, a sober colour

explanation.surface: A fish is set out for a modestly dressed holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish with a venomous spine on its tail.

clue.text: Synopsis Number One returned -—Food Processing

parts.note: a digest is a summary or synopsis

indicators.note: returned means the letters come back in reverse order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A summary of the top food-processing story comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NOI around to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: The body breaks food down chemically in the gut, which is the processing named.

clue.text: Gautier's first is she, in Paris, in ballet?

indicators.note: the first letter of the writer's name is taken

parts.note: elle is French for she

explanation.surface: The heroine of the French writer's ballet is a girl in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: Théophile Gautier co-wrote the story of this 1841 ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: Giselle is a romantic ballet with music by Adolphe Adam.

clue.text: Vehicle needing disinfestation?

explanation.definitionFit: A buggy is a light carriage, and anything crawling with insects is buggy.

clue.text: This stop in speech Times leader got all wrong'

indicators.note: the letters are put wrong, that is, out of order
the leading letter of the newspaper's name is taken

explanation.surface: The Times editorial got everything wrong about speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives T, and 'wrong' rearranges it with GOT and ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A glottal stop is a consonant made by closing the vocal cords, a halt in the voice.

clue.text: Harness coach-horses in tavern outside health 'resort

indicators.note: the inn goes outside, around the resort

parts.note: an inn is a tavern
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: Horses are hitched at an inn serving a spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspan is a South African word, from Afrikaans, for yoking draught animals to a wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspan is to yoke oxen or horses to a vehicle.

clue.text: Is born in London's West End or a foreign capital

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed inside the letters from London

parts.note: the west, or left-hand, end of the written word London is its first three letters
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone born in London's theatreland might instead hail from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: West End is London's theatre district, but here it means the left-hand end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is Portugal's capital, so foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: Mental twist shown by, say, a Levantine animal

parts.note: a kink is a quirk or twist of mind

indicators.note: say signals that the next words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a Jew, the Levant being the eastern Mediterranean region

explanation.surface: An odd quirk is shown by some creature from the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means the two words for a Levantine are heard as the end of the animal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The kinkajou is a tree-dwelling mammal of tropical America related to the raccoon.

clue.text: Endlessly swelling, a song of the country

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a bulge is a swelling
an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: A swelling song of homeland goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the last letter from BULGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulgaria is a nation in south-east Europe on the Black Sea.

clue.text: Shame about general service accommodation, it's filthy

indicators.note: the word for shame goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: 'what a shame' and 'what a pity' mean the same
GS is the abbreviation for general service

explanation.surface: It's a shame how dirty the general barracks are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's filthy' belongs with the definition: a pigsty is accommodation notorious for dirt. 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigsty is a pen for pigs, and by extension any very dirty dwelling.

clue.text: Fatty, Prince Regent as he later was (not hard)

parts.words: Prince Regent as he later was
parts.note: the Prince Regent became King George IV, so Georgius Rex, abbreviated GR
easy means not hard

explanation.surface: The portly Prince Regent's later life was soft.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prince Regent (regent 1811-20) became George IV, famously fat; GR is the royal cipher for a King George.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasy food is oily and full of fat.

clue.text: The merry monarch

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme ruler who was 'a merry old soul', rather than Charles II, usually given this nickname

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Merry Monarch' is the nickname of Charles II, but the nursery-rhyme king is the merry old soul.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme king calls for his pipe, bowl and fiddlers three, a jolly ruler.
